1	# Work — Drain the Queue, Execute, Verify, Close
2	
3	"Doing work" in DDx means draining the ready queue: pick the top ready bead,
4	run one or more `ddx try` attempts, verify the result, and close the bead on
5	success or leave it available for a future eligible retry.
6	
7	## Default surface: `ddx work`
8	
9	```bash
10	ddx work
11	```
12	
13	`ddx work` drains the queue by picking ready beads and invoking `ddx try`.
14	`ddx try` wraps `ddx run`, which is the single agent invocation primitive. DDx
15	owns queue iteration, attempt evidence, and retry policy; the upstream agent
16	owns provider/model routing.
17	
18	Flags worth knowing:
19	
20	- `--once` — pick one bead and stop (don't loop).
21	- `--poll-interval <dur>` — continuous worker mode; wait between
22	  iterations.
23	- `--min-power <n>` / `--max-power <n>` — requested agent power bounds.
24	- `--top-power` — choose a `MinPower` threshold from the agent catalog.
25	- `--harness <name>` / `--provider <name>` / `--model <ref>` — passthrough
26	  constraints only. DDx sends them unchanged and does not route on them.
27	
28	## Primitive: `ddx try`
29	
30	For targeted re-runs, debugging, or running a specific bead:
31	
32	```bash
33	ddx try <bead-id>
34	ddx try <bead-id> --from <rev>      # base commit override
35	ddx try <bead-id> --no-merge        # preserve result, don't land
36	```
37	
38	`ddx try` runs one bead attempt in an isolated git worktree. It calls `ddx run`
39	for the actual agent invocation.
40	
41	## Pick by default, not by ID
42	
43	Under normal operation, **don't specify a bead ID**. `ddx work` picks
44	the top ready bead based on priority + dependency satisfaction. Only
45	pin a specific ID when debugging (`ddx try <id>`) or
46	when the queue ordering would pick the wrong bead and you need to
47	override.
48	
49	## Verify independently before closing
50	
51	**Agents hallucinate successful completions.** Do not trust the
52	agent's self-report. Before closing a bead:
53	
54	1. Run the acceptance-criteria command yourself (from the bead's
55	   `accept:` field). If it's `go test ./foo/...`, run that.
56	2. Check the resulting commit against the in-scope file list from
57	   the bead description. Out-of-scope files touched? Reject the
58	   attempt.
59	3. Read the commit message — does it reference the bead ID?
60	   (`[ddx-<id>]` or similar in the commit subject is the convention.)
61	
62	If all three pass: close the bead.
63	
64	## Close on success, unclaim on failure
65	
66	DDx try/work outcomes form a specific taxonomy. Each outcome
67	maps to a concrete follow-up action:
68	
69	| Outcome | Meaning | Action |
70	|---|---|---|
71	| `success` | Tests pass, AC met, commit landed | `ddx bead close <id>` |
72	| `already_satisfied` | No changes needed (AC was already green) | `ddx bead close <id>` |
73	| `no_changes` | Agent returned without producing commits and wrote `no_changes_rationale.txt` | Leave open, **unclaim** |
74	| `no_evidence_produced` | Agent exited without a commit or rationale | Leave open, **unclaim**, investigate harness/commit failure |
75	| `land_conflict` | Merge conflict on landing the result | Leave open, **unclaim** |
76	| `post_run_check_failed` | Tests or gate failed after landing | Leave open, **unclaim**, investigate |
77	| `execution_failed` | Agent subprocess errored (timeout, crash, provider error) | Leave open, **unclaim** |
78	| `structural_validation_failed` | Result failed structural sanity check | Leave open, **unclaim**, investigate |
79	
80	`ddx work` applies these actions automatically. If you're running
81	`ddx try` directly, apply them manually: `ddx bead update <id>
82	--unclaim` to release a bead after a non-closing outcome, so another
83	worker can pick it up.
84	
85	**Never leave a bead half-owned** — every execution either closes or
86	unclaims.
87	
88	## Testing expectations for bead implementations
89	
90	When an agent implements a bead, its output should include tests
91	that exercise the new code:
92	
93	- **Unit tests** for logic with in-memory stubs for first-party
94	  collaborators. Favor stubs over mocks; mocks that assert on call
95	  sequences test implementation, not behavior.
96	- **Integration tests** against real collaborators where the cost
97	  is small (real git in a temp dir, real DB in a temp file, real
98	  HTTP via a local test server).
99	- **Real e2e tests** at the outermost boundary. E2e tests that mock
100	  the database or the network are unit tests lying about their
101	  scope.
102	- **Coverage measurement only where the project tracks it.** Don't
103	  introduce coverage tooling just for one bead; use what the
104	  project already has. Coverage is a signal, not a target.
105	- **Performance claims require baselines.** If the bead's AC
106	  mentions "faster" or "scales", the acceptance test must include:
107	  (a) a numeric baseline, (b) an explicit boundary (what's
108	  measured, what's excluded), (c) a reproducible harness.
109	
110	## Anti-patterns
111	
112	- **Trusting the agent's "done"**: always re-run the AC command
113	  yourself before closing.
114	- **Closing on no_changes/no_evidence**: only `success` and `already_satisfied`
115	  close a bead. `no_changes` requires an explicit rationale. `no_evidence_produced`
116	  means the agent returned without a commit or rationale — unclaim and investigate.
117	- **Squashing bead-attempt commits**: the per-attempt history is
118	  an audit trail (evidence commits, heartbeats). Use only
119	  `git merge --ff-only` or `--no-ff`; never squash/rebase/filter.
120	- **Running passthrough pins without a reason**: power-bound dispatch lets the
121	  agent choose an appropriate route. Use `--harness`, `--provider`, or
122	  `--model` only for explicit operator constraints, bug repros, or controlled
123	  tests.
124	- **Parallel workers on the same claimed bead**: the tracker
125	  guards against this via claim semantics, but don't try to defeat
126	  it — each claim represents an in-flight attempt.
127	
128	## CLI reference
129	
130	```bash
131	ddx work                                    # default queue drain
132	ddx work --once                             # one bead, then stop
133	ddx work --poll-interval 30s                # continuous worker
134	ddx work --min-power 10                     # request stronger attempts
135	ddx work --harness claude                   # passthrough constraint
136	
137	ddx try <id>                                # one bead attempt
138	ddx try <id> --from <rev>                   # override base commit
139	ddx try <id> --no-merge                     # preserve iteration
140	```
141	
142	Full flag list: `ddx work --help`, `ddx try --help`, `ddx run --help`.
143

12	# Solution Design: SD-010 — Multi-Harness × Model Matrix Benchmark
13	
14	**Bead**: agent-fab7feae (Author SD-010 — Multi-Harness × Model Matrix Benchmark)
15	**Type**: Design spec (normative)
16	**Status**: Draft — superseded for official fiz-wrapper comparisons by
17	`terminalbench-fiz-wrapper-comparison-2026-05-06`; retained as implementation
18	reference for matrix runner mechanics, telemetry, aggregation, and publication
19	rules.
20	
21	---
22	
23	## 1. Summary
24	
25	This spec originally governed the **multi-harness × model matrix benchmark**:
26	TerminalBench-2 runs that compare fiz against other CLI agent harnesses
27	(initial tranche: `pi`, `opencode`) on a shared anchor model and a shared task
28	subset, and that extend in later tranches to a second model and to
29	frontier-reference cells (`codex`, `claude-code`).
30	
31	The official comparison architecture changed on 2026-05-06. Official
32	TerminalBench cells now run through one Harbor installed agent,
33	`scripts/benchmark/harbor_agent.py:FizeauAgent`, and select the execution path
34	with fiz pins such as `FIZEAU_HARNESS=claude`, `FIZEAU_HARNESS=codex`,
35	`FIZEAU_HARNESS=pi`, `FIZEAU_HARNESS=opencode`, or
36	`FIZEAU_PROVIDER=openrouter`. Raw per-harness Harbor adapters may remain as
37	diagnostics, but they are not the official comparison path.
38	
39	This document remains normative for reusable mechanics only:
40	
41	- matrix run state machine
42	- failure taxonomy
43	- aggregation outputs
44	- cost reporting
45	- reproducibility metadata
46	- same-model-different-harness caveats
47	
48	**Relation to existing specs.** SD-010 *extends*, it does not replace:
49	
50	- **SD-008** (Terminal-Bench / Harbor integration audit) governs the in-container
51	  `BaseInstalledAgent` integration path. SD-010 is amended into SD-008 §6
52	  ("Multi-Harness Extension") and reuses the in-container layout for every
53	  harness in the matrix. Harnesses that cannot be installed in-container are
54	  documented and dropped — never run host-side.
55	- **SD-009** (fiz Benchmark Mode) governs single-harness fiz
56	  evaluation. Its §5 thresholds (resolved-task floor 0.55, target 0.7) are
57	  **scoped to fiz's own runs only**. Cross-harness cells use **mean reward
58	  ± SD over reps (minimum 3 reps per cell)** and are not gated by those
59	  thresholds. SD-009 §7.1 cross-references SD-010 for the multi-harness
60	  publication policy and §9 lifts the resumability / failure taxonomy normatively.
61	- **FEAT-005** (Logging and Cost) is amended to acknowledge the four token
62	  streams (input, output, cached-input, retried-input) tracked under SD-010,
63	  and to source $-per-Mtok numbers from the SD-010 profile schema rather than
64	  an ad-hoc per-runner constant.
65	
66	The ground truth for the architecture and decisions in this spec is the planning
67	artifact `docs/research/harness-matrix-plan-2026-04-29.md` (v7, codex peer
68	reviewed v2 + v6). That plan closes once the epic bead is filed; subsequent
69	revisions live here in SD-010.
70	
71	**Central caveat (must restate in every published memo).** "Same model,
72	different harness" is *not* a clean control of model capability. Each harness
73	ships its own system prompt, tool schema, retry policy, reasoning effort,
74	context compaction, and default sampling. Matrix results compare *(harness
75	scaffolding + policy) over a shared model API*, not pure harness skill, and
76	not pure model skill.
77	
78	---
79	
80	## 2. Architectural Decisions D1–D6 (Normative)
81	
82	The following decisions are lifted verbatim from `harness-matrix-plan-2026-04-29.md`
83	and are normative for every implementation bead under this spec.
84	
85	### D1. In-container only
86	
87	All harness cells run inside the upstream Harbor container. Mixing host-side
88	and in-container layouts contaminates the comparison. Harnesses that can't be
89	installed in-container are dropped from the matrix (documented in the OSS
90	harness install spike), not run host-side.
91	
92	### D2. Single CLI entry: `fiz-bench matrix`
93	
94	2026-05-06 amendment: the single entry still applies, but official cells should
95	pass only the `fiz` Harbor adapter/installed agent and vary the fiz target via
96	profile/env pins. Historical examples below that pass `--harnesses=fiz,pi,...`
97	are retained as diagnostic-run examples and must not be used for official
98	fiz-wrapper comparison claims.
99	
100	A Go subcommand replaces the parallel-shell-scripts approach. It reuses the
101	existing TB subset loader and harness registry; it shells out to `harbor run`
102	once per run.
103	
104	```
105	fiz-bench matrix \
106	  --subset=scripts/beadbench/external/termbench-subset-canary.json \
107	  --profiles=gpt-5-mini \
108	  --harnesses=fiz,pi,opencode \
109	  --reps=3 \
110	  --budget-usd=15 \
111	  --out=benchmark-results/matrix-<ts>/ \
112	  [--resume] [--force-rerun] [--retry-budget-halted]
113	```
114	
115	No `--concurrency` flag in v1 — see D6.
116	
117	### D3. Smoke vs matrix split
118	
119	The existing `cmd/bench --external=termbench` path **survives** as
120	`--mode=smoke` — fast, ungraded, host tempdir, useful while iterating on
121	fiz code. The matrix subcommand is the **only** graded multi-harness
122	path. The smoke path MUST NOT be used to produce cross-harness comparison
123	memos.
124	
125	### D4. Run state machine and telemetry schema
126	
127	A run has three orthogonal axes; `final_status` is derived from them
128	deterministically. Adapters report the first two; the runner derives the
129	third.
130	
131	```
132	process_outcome  ∈ {completed, timeout, harness_crash, install_failed, harness_refused, budget_halted}
133	grading_outcome  ∈ {graded, ungraded}                # ungraded = no verifier output
134	reward           ∈ {0, 1, null}                      # null iff ungraded
135	
136	final_status (derived)
137	  = graded_pass            if grading_outcome=graded ∧ reward=1
138	  = graded_fail            if grading_outcome=graded ∧ reward=0
139	  = budget_halted          if process_outcome=budget_halted
140	  = install_fail_permanent if process_outcome=install_failed ∧ retriable=false
141	  = install_fail_transient if process_outcome=install_failed ∧ retriable=true
142	  = ran_ungraded           if grading_outcome=ungraded ∧ process_outcome=completed
143	  = <process_outcome>      otherwise                 # timeout, harness_crash, harness_refused
144	```

23	## Egress Canary (rig validation, before any new adapter work)
24	
25	`egress_canary.sh` proves in-container egress to a tool-capable smoke
26	provider before spending budget on full benchmarks or building new
27	adapters. It targets a single concrete TB-2 task (`fix-git` by default —
28	the bead-pinned canary; terminal-bench@2.0 has no `hello-world` task at
29	the pinned commit) and accepts an **egress signal** (trajectory.json with
30	≥ 1 step) as success. The verifier reward is recorded but is *not* part
31	of the gate, since smoke models routinely fail TB-2 tasks.
32	
33	```bash
34	OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-... ./scripts/benchmark/egress_canary.sh
35	```
36	
37	Output: `benchmark-results/egress-canary-<UTC-TIMESTAMP>/` containing the
38	trajectory, reward, a `trial/` symlink, and a `canary.json` summary.

136	## Evidence Workflow
137	
138	The benchmark evidence pipeline is:
139	
140	1. Run a benchmark job and keep the raw artifacts in `benchmark-results/`.
141	2. Import the resulting run, report, or curated snapshot into JSONL evidence.
142	3. Validate the imported evidence and append it to an append-only ledger.
143	4. Generate benchmark-specific or cross-benchmark claims from the ledger.
144	
145	The canonical operator loop for a TerminalBench matrix is:
146	
147	```bash
148	# 1) produce raw matrix artifacts
149	OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-... \
150	  scripts/benchmark/run_medium_model_terminalbench_comparison.sh canary
151	
152	# 2) project raw matrix artifacts into normalized evidence
153	go run ./cmd/bench evidence import-terminalbench --matrix <matrix-dir> --out benchmark-results/evidence/terminalbench.jsonl
154	
155	# 3) validate and append to the ledger
156	go run ./cmd/bench evidence validate benchmark-results/evidence/terminalbench.jsonl
157	go run ./cmd/bench evidence append --in benchmark-results/evidence/terminalbench.jsonl --ledger benchmark-results/evidence/ledger.jsonl
158	
159	# 4) emit benchmark claims from the ledger
160	go run ./cmd/bench fhi delta --ledger benchmark-results/evidence/ledger.jsonl --left <record_id> --right <record_id>
161	go run ./cmd/bench fhi rank --ledger benchmark-results/evidence/ledger.jsonl
162	```
163	
164	This workflow is anchored by [SD-012](../../docs/helix/02-design/solution-designs/SD-012-benchmark-evidence-ledger.md)
165	and the benchmark resource notes for
166	[Rapid-MLX MHI](../../docs/resources/rapid-mlx-mhi-2026-05-06.md),
167	[SkillsBench](../../docs/resources/skillsbench-2026-05-06.md),
168	[SWE-bench](../../docs/resources/swebench-2026-05-06.md), and
169	[HumanEval](../../docs/resources/humaneval-2026-05-06.md).
170	
171	Beadbench enters the same ledger path through `evidence import-beadbench` from
172	its `report.json` output, and curated external snapshots enter through
173	`evidence import-external`. For a concrete beadbench source-run example, see
174	[the OMLX Qwen reasoning sweep note](../../docs/research/beadbench-omlx-qwen-reasoning-sweep-2026-04-24.md).
175	
176	Use the command family below for the full evidence loop:
177	
178	- `go run ./cmd/bench evidence import-terminalbench`
179	- `go run ./cmd/bench evidence import-beadbench`
180	- `go run ./cmd/bench evidence import-external`
181	- `go run ./cmd/bench evidence validate`
182	- `go run ./cmd/bench evidence append`
183	- `go run ./cmd/bench fhi delta`
184	- `go run ./cmd/bench fhi rank`

1	# Benchmark corpus
2	
3	The internal benchmark corpus is a *curated*, capability-tagged set of
4	closed beads worth tracking over time. It feeds the beadbench harness
5	(see `scripts/beadbench/`) and gives us a stable, named pool of tasks
6	for harness-vs-harness and model-vs-model comparisons.
7	
8	The curation **is** the value. The corpus is intentionally not
9	auto-promoted. Promotion is a deliberate human act, gated on the
10	question "does this bead teach us something the rest of the corpus
11	does not?".
12	
13	## File layout
14	
15	Three files, all under `scripts/beadbench/`:
16	
17	```
18	scripts/beadbench/
19	  corpus.yaml                       # append-only top-level index
20	  corpus/
21	    capabilities.yaml               # controlled-vocabulary tags
22	    <bead-id>.yaml                  # per-bead detail (one per index entry)
23	```
24	
25	### `corpus.yaml`
26	
27	Top-level index. Append-only. Each entry has:
28	
29	| field          | required | notes |
30	| -------------- | -------- | ----- |
31	| `id`           | yes      | bead id (e.g. `agent-39f79181`) |
32	| `capability`   | one of   | tag from `capabilities.yaml` (kind=capability) |
33	| `failure_mode` | one of   | tag from `capabilities.yaml` (kind=failure_mode) |
34	| `promoted`     | yes      | `YYYY-MM-DD` |
35	| `promoted_by`  | yes      | identity recording the promotion |
36	
37	Exactly one of `capability` / `failure_mode` must be set.
38	
39	### `corpus/<bead-id>.yaml`
40	
41	Per-bead detail. One file per index entry; the file's `bead_id` must
42	match an entry in `corpus.yaml`. Required fields: `bead_id`,
43	`project_root`, `base_rev` (pre-change), `known_good_rev`
44	(resolution), `captured`, `difficulty` (`easy|medium|hard`),
45	`prompt_kind` (`implement-with-spec|port-by-analogy|debug-and-fix|review`),
46	and the same `capability` or `failure_mode` tag as the index. `notes`
47	is free text describing what makes the bead instructive.
48	
49	### `corpus/capabilities.yaml`
50	
51	Controlled vocabulary. Adding a tag here is the *only* way to use it
52	in `corpus.yaml`. Each tag declares an `id`, an `area` (cli, provider,
53	harness, catalog, routing, prompt, …), a `kind`
54	(`capability` or `failure_mode`), and a description.
55	
56	## Curation rules
57	
58	A bead earns a slot in the corpus when **all** of the following hold:
59	
60	1. The bead is closed and has a reachable resolution rev (either
61	   `closing_commit_sha` on the bead record, or one we can name with
62	   confidence — multi-commit slices are allowed if the final commit is
63	   identifiable).
64	2. The bead exemplifies a `capability` or `failure_mode` we want to
65	   regression-track. Routine refactors, doc updates, and trivial fixes
66	   do not qualify, no matter how clean the diff is.
67	3. Promotion adds signal that the rest of the corpus does not already
68	   carry. If we already have a sampler-resolver capability bead, the
69	   second sampler-resolver bead is *probably* not worth promoting unless
70	   it covers a meaningfully different surface (e.g. a different
71	   provider seam).
72	
73	If the bead is being promoted because the agent *failed* on it,
74	the entry uses `failure_mode` (not `capability`). Failure-mode entries
75	are valuable: they say "this is the surface the agent has historically
76	tripped on; treat regressions on this kind of task as model-quality
77	evidence".
78	
79	## Promoting a bead
80	
81	The `ddx-agent corpus promote` subcommand handles the gate, the writes,
82	and the post-write validation:
83	
84	```
85	ddx-agent corpus promote agent-39f79181 \
86	  --capability sampling-resolver-cli-wiring \
87	  --difficulty medium \
88	  --prompt-kind implement-with-spec \
89	  --notes "Catches CLI-side resolver wiring + telemetry plumbing." \
90	  --yes
91	```
92	
93	What the command does:
94	
95	- Refuses if the bead is already in `corpus.yaml`.
96	- Refuses if the bead is not closed in `.ddx/beads.jsonl`.
97	- Defaults `base_rev` to the bead's `parent_commit_sha` and
98	  `known_good_rev` to its `closing_commit_sha`. Override with
99	  `--base-rev` / `--known-good-rev` for multi-commit slices.
100	- Defaults `project_root` to the workdir and `promoted_by` to `$USER`.
101	- Without `--yes`, shows the plan and asks for confirmation.
102	- Writes both files atomically (temp + rename). Validates after write;
103	  if validation fails, both writes are rolled back and the command
104	  returns the validation error.
105	
106	`ddx-agent corpus validate` re-runs the cross-validator at any time.
107	`ddx-agent corpus list` shows the index in a tabular format
108	(`--json` for machine output).
109	
110	## Filtering beadbench by corpus
111	
112	`scripts/beadbench/run_beadbench.py` accepts two corpus-aware flags:
113	
114	- `--corpus-only` — restrict the task set to beads whose `bead_id`
115	  appears in `corpus.yaml`. Useful for reproducible apples-to-apples
116	  arm comparisons.
117	- `--capability=<tag>` — restrict to corpus beads tagged with the
118	  given capability (or failure_mode). Useful for "how do these arms do
119	  on this surface specifically?" investigations.
120	
121	Both filters are pure intersections: a task must already exist in
122	`manifest-v1.json` for it to be considered. A capability tag with no
123	matching task in the manifest produces an empty selection.
124	
125	## Why curated, not automatic?
126	
127	The corpus is an editorial artifact. Auto-promotion would either:
128	
129	- Promote everything (adds noise, dilutes signal — most beads are not
130	  instructive enough to be worth a regression test), or
131	- Promote on some heuristic (commit size, test coverage delta, etc.)
132	  that is easy to game and hard to interpret.
133	
134	Curation forces us to articulate, in the bead's `notes` field, *why*
135	this bead is worth tracking. That articulation is the corpus's

8	# External Benchmark Adapters
9	
10	This document describes the pattern for adding external benchmark suites
11	(TerminalBench today; SWE-bench / AgentBench / others tomorrow) to the
12	`cmd/bench` runner. The goal is to publish numbers comparable to what
13	pi / codex / claude-code report, by using each upstream benchmark's own
14	rubric — not a homegrown re-implementation of it.
15	
16	## Design principles
17	
18	1. **Use the upstream grader unmodified.** The whole point of an external
19	   benchmark is the published rubric; reimplementing it would produce
20	   incomparable scores. Adapters translate our agent surface into the
21	   upstream harness contract (input format, harness-output paths) and let
22	   the upstream verifier compute the verdict.
23	
24	2. **Submodule, not vendor.** Task corpora are large, churn upstream, and
25	   are sometimes licensed differently. Pin a commit via git submodule
26	   under `scripts/benchmark/external/<benchmark>/`. Never copy tasks into
27	   the agent tree.
28	
29	3. **Frozen subset for routine runs.** The full corpus is too expensive
30	   for every release. Each adapter ships a 20–50 task subset under
31	   `scripts/beadbench/external/<benchmark>-subset.json`. Inclusion
32	   criteria are documented in the file's top-level `_comment` field.
33	   Bumping the subset version requires a fresh baseline run.
34	
35	4. **Separation of concerns.**
36	   - `internal/benchmark/external/<benchmark>/` — Go adapter package
37	     that parses task format, builds `ServiceExecuteRequest`, and
38	     captures harness events into the upstream's expected output shape.
39	   - `cmd/bench` — CLI glue (`--external=<name>`) that loads the
40	     subset, drives the adapter, writes per-run results.
41	   - `scripts/benchmark/external/<benchmark>/` — submodule with the
42	     upstream task corpus.
43	   - `scripts/benchmark/<runner>.sh` — optional wrapper that invokes
44	     the upstream verifier (e.g. `harbor run ...` for TerminalBench).
45	
46	5. **Don't fake passing tests.** When the upstream verifier is unavailable
47	   (no Docker, etc.) the adapter writes the harness output and reports
48	   `status: ran` with no `reward` field. Only when an upstream verifier
49	   has dropped a `reward.txt` does the adapter report a graded outcome.
50	
51	## Pattern (per benchmark)
52	
53	| File / dir                                                      | Role                                                                    |
54	| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
55	| `internal/benchmark/external/<bench>/doc.go`                    | What the adapter does and (importantly) does *not* do                   |
56	| `internal/benchmark/external/<bench>/task.go`                   | Parse upstream task definitions into a Go `Task` type                   |
57	| `internal/benchmark/external/<bench>/plan.go`                   | Build `agent.ServiceExecuteRequest` + per-task timeout                  |
58	| `internal/benchmark/external/<bench>/trajectory.go`             | Fold `harnesses.Event` stream into upstream's expected output schema    |
59	| `internal/benchmark/external/<bench>/grader.go`                 | Read upstream verifier's verdict files; never reimplement scoring       |
60	| `cmd/bench/external_<bench>.go`                                 | CLI orchestration: subset → adapter → service.Execute → results.json    |
61	| `scripts/benchmark/external/<bench>/`                           | Git submodule pinned to a known-good upstream commit                    |
62	| `scripts/beadbench/external/<bench>-subset.json`                | Frozen subset of 20–50 task IDs with selection rule                     |
63	| `benchmark-results/<bench>/<run-id>/`                           | Per-run output (created by the runner; gitignored)                      |
64	| `docs/research/external-benchmark-baseline-<date>.md`           | Baseline matrix (one per published number)                              |
65	
66	## TerminalBench reference implementation
67	
68	Bead `agent-6d6ae2f6` introduced this. Highlights:
69	
70	- **Task format.** TerminalBench tasks are a directory containing
71	  `task.yaml`, `tests/test_outputs.py`, a `Dockerfile`, and a solution
72	  script. Our adapter reads `task.yaml` for the instruction text and
73	  timeouts; the Dockerfile and tests stay upstream.
74	- **Output contract.** Harbor's grader expects ATIF v1.4 trajectory at
75	  `<out>/logs/agent/trajectory.json` and reads reward from
76	  `<out>/logs/verifier/reward.txt`. The adapter writes the former and
77	  reads the latter; it never produces reward.
78	- **Submodule.** `scripts/benchmark/external/terminal-bench-2/` pinned at
79	  `53ff2b87d621bdb97b455671f2bd9728b7d86c11`. (Note: the upstream URL
80	  drifted from `terminal-bench` → `terminal-bench-2`; SD-008 §1 records
81	  the audit. We use TB2 because it is the actively-graded dataset.)
82	- **Subset.** 20 tasks under `scripts/beadbench/external/termbench-subset.json`,
83	  same IDs as the evidence-grade comparison subset
84	  (`scripts/benchmark/task-subset-v2.yaml`) plus 5 cheap easy tasks for
85	  smoke runs.
86	- **Invocation.**
87	
88	  ```sh
89	  ddx-agent-bench run \
90	    --external=termbench \
91	    --external-harness=ddx-agent \
92	    --external-model=openrouter/qwen/qwen3.6-plus \
93	    --external-max-tasks=3
94	  ```
95	
96	- **Grading.** After the bench command finishes, run
97	  `scripts/benchmark/run_benchmark.sh` to invoke Harbor's verifier
98	  (Docker required; see SD-008 §5). The verifier drops reward.txt under
99	  each task's output directory; a re-run of `ddx-agent-bench run
100	  --external=termbench` then surfaces the reward in `results.json`.
101	
102	## Adding a new benchmark
103	
104	1. Open a sister bead (don't bundle multiple benchmarks in one PR).
105	2. Audit the upstream task format and grader contract; record findings
106	   in a new SD-### document.
107	3. Add the submodule under `scripts/benchmark/external/<name>/` pinned
108	   to a specific commit.
109	4. Implement the adapter package mirroring the TerminalBench layout above.
110	5. Define the frozen subset with documented inclusion criteria.
111	6. Wire `cmd/bench --external=<name>`.
112	7. Run a 3–5 task baseline on at least three arms and write up
113	   `docs/research/external-benchmark-baseline-<date>.md`.
114	
115	## Evidence Ledger Obligation
116	
117	Every new benchmark adapter or importer must also define how its source results
118	project into the benchmark evidence ledger described by
119	`solution-designs/SD-012-benchmark-evidence-ledger.md`.
120	
121	The adapter/importer plan must explicitly state:
122	
123	- benchmark name/version and dataset commit or capture timestamp
124	- score metric and normalization
125	- subject identity fields: model, harness, provider, endpoint, and deployment
126	  class
127	- version fields for Fizeau, harness wrapper, harness CLI/runtime, provider
128	  surface, model snapshot, and benchmark/scorer
129	- source artifact paths and hashes
130	- session-log and trajectory linkage when the run is executed through Fizeau
131	- invalid-run taxonomy and denominator handling
132	- whether the benchmark can contribute to FHI, catalog model power, or both
133	
134	Do not add a new benchmark runner that produces only benchmark-specific output
135	without a ledger projection bead.
136	
137	## What stays out of scope
138	
139	- Internal beadbench is unaffected — `--external=...` is opt-in.
140	- We do not republish upstream task content; only adapter glue and
141	  results.
142	- We do not score with our own metrics on top of external rewards
143	  unless explicitly requested. The published external rubric is the
144	  signal; layering anything on top changes the comparison.
